prompt: Which of these does NOT prove that two triangles are congruent?

choices.label: AAA — all three pairs of angles are congruent
ASA — two angles and the side between them
SSS — all three pairs of sides
AAS — two angles and a side not between them

hint: Congruence is about size AND shape. Which choice never mentions a single length?

hints.text: Congruence is about size AND shape. Which choice never mentions a single length?
Matching angles alone fix the shape but say nothing about how big the triangle is.
AAA does not prove congruence — it only proves similarity.

explanation: Every valid congruence criterion (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL) includes at least one side, because a side sets the size.
AAA includes no sides, so the triangles could be the same shape at wildly different scales.
AAA therefore proves similarity, not congruence.

alternativeExplanations.title: A concrete counterexample
steps: A triangle with angles $60^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$60^\circ$ and sides of 2 cm matches all three angles of one with sides of 200 cm.
Same angles, wildly different triangles — so AAA cannot be a congruence criterion.
